sections.label: Helping Singaporeans own homes
sections.summary: The passage states that helping Singaporeans own homes involves building public housing, pricing flats affordably with grants, and maintaining a stable property market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: This has been the work of several generations and we will continue to work hard to deliver this commitment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We help Singaporeans own their homes by: (a) building public housing in step with demand; (b) by pricing new flats affordably and providing generous grants to first-time buyers; and (c) by maintaining a stable and sustainable property market where asset values increase in tandem with economic growth.

sections.label: BTO applicants during pandemic
sections.summary: Over the pandemic's last three years, first-time BTO applicants rose 80% and second-time applicants rose 140% versus 2017 to 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Over the last three years of the pandemic, first-time BTO applicants increased by 80% and second-time BTO applicants grew even more by a whopping 140%, compared to the preceding three years from 2017 to 2019, pre-pandemic.

sections.label: Up to 100,000 new flats
sections.summary: Between 2021 and 2025, up to 100,000 new flats will be launched in total if needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Between 2021 and 2025, in total, we will launch up to 100,000 new flats if needed.

sections.label: 4-room flats for first-timer families
sections.summary: Since August last year, at least 95% of 4-room and larger BTO flats were set aside for first-timer families, with prices kept almost flat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Since August last year, we have set aside at least 95% of 4-room and larger BTO flats for FT families, both in mature and non-mature estates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Despite strong demand and rising construction costs in these past two years, we have kept BTO prices almost flat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In 2019, a 4-room BTO flat in a non-mature estate was priced at $341,000 on average before grants.

sections.label: Enhanced CPF Housing Grant
sections.summary: Eligible first-timers can receive the Enhanced CPF Housing Grant of up to $80,000, with more grants for lower incomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Eligible first-timers can enjoy the Enhanced CPF Housing Grant (EHG) of up to $80,000, with more in grants provided to those with lower incomes.

sections.label: Affordable BTO flats for households
sections.summary: Close to 70% of BTO flats launched in 2022 can be affordably purchased by households earning $8,400 at an MSR of 25% or less.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Close to 70% of the BTO flats that were launched last year, 2022, across all estates can be affordably purchased with a household income of $8,400 at a MSR of 25% or less, meaning that these households use a quarter or less of their household income to pay for the mortgage instalment.

sections.label: Housing price to income ratios
sections.summary: In London, Los Angeles and Sydney, housing costs between eight and 15 times total household income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In London, Los Angeles and Sydney, it is between eight and 15 times income, so between eight and 15 years of total household income.

sections.label: Young couples mature estate BTO
sections.summary: Many young couples fail to secure a BTO flat because they seek mature estates, with first-timer applications about 1.6 times non-mature estates in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Many young couples have not been successful in securing a BTO flat because they are trying hard to secure one in a mature estate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: This can be seen from the first-timer BTO applications to mature estates which is about 1.6 times that to non-mature estates in 2022.

sections.label: New flat supply and SWT flats
sections.summary: Up to 100,000 new flats will be launched from 2021 to 2025, with more Shorter Waiting Time flats from 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In terms of supply, we are committed to launching up to 100,000 new flats between 2021 and 2025 if needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Once we get over this current challenge, we intend to launch more Shorter Waiting Time (SWT) flats from 2024 onwards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We aim to reach pre-COVID-19 levels by launching around 2,000 to 3,000 SWT flats per year by 2025, with waiting times of under three years.

sections.label: Accessible affordable housing for generations
sections.summary: Housing must stay accessible and affordable for current and future generations, so the government disagrees with PSP's Motion and tables its own.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: They must enable us to continue providing Singaporeans with accessible, affordable housing not just now or for the next election term, but decade after decade, for the next generation of Singaporeans and the generations after that.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: That is why we disagree with the Progress Singapore Party’s (PSP) implicit claims in its Motion and decided to table our own.

sections.label: HDB Home Ownership Programme deficit
sections.summary: In the last financial year, HDB incurred a deficit of $3.85 billion on its Home Ownership Programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In the last financial year, HDB incurred a deficit of $3.85 billion on its Home Ownership Programme.

sections.label: Land sales proceeds go to reserves
sections.summary: Land is part of the reserves, so land sale proceeds go back to the reserves, not to the current Government as revenue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: More importantly, land is part of our reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Proceeds from land sales do not come to the current Government as revenue for spending.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The proceeds go back to the reserves in order to preserve the value of the reserves.

sections.label: New flat supply commitment
sections.summary: The government commits to launch up to 100,000 new flats from 2021 to 2025 and around 2,000 to 3,000 Shorter Waiting Time flats yearly from 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In terms of supply, we are committed to launch up to 100,000 new flats between 2021 and 2025 if needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We also intend to launch around 2,000 to 3,000 Shorter Waiting Time (SWT) flats per year from 2025 onwards.
